title: Period summary, version 2
description:
One reporting day or month, aggregated from saved digests. Stored at `digests/daily-summaries/{yyyy-mm-dd}.json` and `digests/monthly-summaries/{yyyy-mm}.json`.

A day aggregates call digests; a month aggregates DAY SUMMARIES, not calls. That hierarchy is what keeps a month cheap, and it is also why `sources` has to say how complete it was: a month built from 28 of 31 days is not a quiet month.

The aggregation rules this shape exists to enforce:

- Every count names its denominator (`outcomeCounts.evaluated`). No bare rates are stored; the UI divides, and can therefore show the denominator beside the figure.
- Affected call and client counts are UNIONS over identity, so re-reading a source cannot double-count.
- A month sums numerators and denominators from its days. It never averages daily percentages, because a 2% day with 10 sessions and a 2% day with 10,000 are not equal evidence.
- Percentiles and distributions are not aggregated at all unless they are mergeable. Where a figure cannot be merged honestly the field is absent and the UI shows it unavailable.
- Classification buckets are disjoint and are never summed to get 'affected clients'.

affected.description: Drilldown. For each check that anything failed, which calls and which client sessions to open.

id.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, `YYYY-MM` for a month.

timezone.description: UTC, always. Not configurable: a reporting day has to mean one thing across storage, aggregation and the page, and server-absolute time is the only definition that survives clients in other zones and a browser with a wrong clock.

provisional.description: True while the period can still gain data — the current day, or the current month. A provisional summary is correct for what it has read and is expected to change, which is a different statement from incomplete.

sources.title: What this was built from, and what was missed
sources.description: The field that makes a partial period impossible to misread as an empty one. `complete` is false whenever anything was found and not read, or expected and not found.

kind.description: `calls` for a day, `days` for a month.

failures.description: Why each unread source was unread. Distinguishes a missing object, an invalid one, and one written by a schema version this build does not implement — three different operator actions.

missingDays.description: Months only: days in the month with no summary at all. A day that genuinely had no calls still gets a summary, so a day listed here is an unprocessed day, not a quiet one.

id.description: The callId or the day id that could not be read.

calls.description: Distinct callIds read. A union, so a rebuild cannot inflate it.

callSeconds.description: Summed call wall-clock duration. Kept separate from the client-second figures above on purpose: they are not comparable and a page that mixes them reports impaired time exceeding elapsed time.

counts.description: Over client sessions, with `evaluated` as the denominator.

callsAffected.description: Distinct calls with at least one failing client session. A union over callId, never a sum of per-day values.

failedSeconds.description: Summed assessed client-seconds inside failing intervals. Absent where the rule has no interval, and absent in a month if any contributing day lacked it — a partial sum would read as a smaller problem.

classificationCounts.title: Client sessions by what their evidence amounts to
classificationCounts.description: Disjoint. These four sum to `totals.clientSessions`, which is the only sum that is valid here — adding any subset to get 'affected clients' double-counts, because a session is classified once by its strongest evidence.

trend.title: Quality across the period
trend.description: Hour buckets for a day, day buckets for a month. Each bucket carries its own denominator so an hour with two sessions is not drawn as confidently as an hour with two hundred.

clientSessionsFailed.description: Sessions with at least one failing check. Assigned to the bucket the session STARTED in, matching the call-to-day rule, so one session is counted once.

clientSessions.description: The full roomId+callId+clientId triple, so the UI builds /{roomId}/{callId}/{clientId} without opening a single call digest.

truncated.description: True when the lists above were capped. A capped list is a navigation aid, not a count — read `counts` and `callsAffected` for the numbers.
